title: Kena Upanishad (one week): who impels the mind? (7 of 7)
hook: Uma answers: it was Brahman, and the victory was never yours
tomorrow: Katha Upanishad (one week): Nachiketa and Death (1 of 7)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the story of the gods and Brahman went on: the wind couldn't move the grass, the being vanished before Indra, and Uma Haimavati appeared. Today, her answer. Day two hundred forty-five.

Sometimes the truth about a thing only arrives afterward. A grown woman learns that a teacher quietly paid her school fees. A son learns that his parents skipped meals so he could eat. And every memory of those years rearranges itself: oh. It was you, all along. Indra is standing in empty space, beside a radiant woman, and he asks her what that wondrous being was. Her answer rearranges the whole story.
screen: `IT WAS YOU, ALL ALONG.` → `INDRA ASKS.` → `UMA ANSWERS.`

segments.voice: Section four. Uma says: it is Brahman. It was in Brahman's victory that you were glorying. And then Indra knew. That's the whole reveal. The victory the gods called ours was Brahman's. The fire that could burn and the wind that could carry were Brahman's power, lent. The text adds that Agni, Vayu and Indra stand above the other gods because they came nearest to it, and Indra above them all, because he was the first to know it was Brahman. Then the teaching turns inward. How is Brahman glimpsed? Like a flash of lightning. Like the blink of an eye: ah! Brahman isn't held; it flashes, and you're changed. And in yourself? The mind moves toward it, and remembers it, again and again. Then a name to hold onto: tadvanam, which Shankara reads as the one who is adored, the dear one. Meditate on it as the beloved, the text says, and all beings will love such a person. Finally the student asks: teach me the Upanishad. The teacher says: it's been taught. Its foundation is discipline, self-control and work. The Vedas are its limbs. Truth is its home. So here's the week. By whom does the mind fly out? The ear of the ear. The eye doesn't go there. Unknown to those who claim to know. The gods take credit, fire can't burn a blade of grass, wind can't lift it, the king comes near and is given a teacher. And Uma: it was Brahman. The one behind the ear, the one behind the victory, all along.
screen: `IT WAS BRAHMAN'S VICTORY.` · `LIKE A FLASH OF LIGHTNING.` · `TADVANAM: THE DEAR ONE.` · `TRUTH IS ITS HOME.` · then, large: `THE ONE BEHIND THE EAR.`

segments.voice: Two minutes. Think back over this week. Pick one moment when you felt something flash: a sound you really heard, a flinch that softened, a question that opened. Hold it the way the Kena says the mind holds Brahman: coming back to it, again and again. Each time your attention wanders, return to that moment, gently, like returning to someone dear. The bell holds the time.
Tadvana, the one who is adored, the dear one. Uma told Indra: it is Brahman; the victory you were glorying in was Brahman's. Meditate on it as the beloved.
Your line: the one behind the ear. That's the Kena. Tomorrow, a boy walks into the house of Death. Today, thank someone whose help you didn't see at the time. Day two hundred forty-five.

howItsDone: In Vedanta study the Kena is read with commentaries such as Shankara's; Uma's answer, 'it is Brahman', marks the moment the gods learn their power was never their own.

fork.setup: Indra asks Uma: what was that wondrous being? what does she say?
options: 'it is Brahman; the victory was its, not yours.'
fork.reveal: it is Brahman. in Brahman's victory you were glorying. and then Indra knew.

original.note: Sanskrit: tadvana, read by Shankara as the one who is adored, the dear one; Kena 4.6.

trapdoor: what you thought: the gods are the heroes of the story.
what it means: every power the gods had was Brahman's; the story acts out the ear of the ear.
what a scholar hears: Kena 4.4's lightning image is read by some as the glimpse of Brahman in nature and 4.5's remembering as its glimpse in the self (adhidaivata / adhyatma).

sources.ref: Kena Upanishad 4.7–4.8 (the foundation of the teaching; truth its home)
